S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.

subtypes.Derailment or Loose Associations: A speech pattern of switching rapidly from one topic to another with no logical connection between thoughts.
subtypes.Tangentiality: Speech that deviates entirely from the question and fails to answer directly.
subtypes.Incoherence or Word Salad: Severe fragmentation of speech and sentence structure, making it nearly impossible to understand.
subtypes.Neologisms: Using made-up words that have meaning only to the individual.
subtypes.Clang Associations: Speech governed by sounds, such as rhyming, rather than the meaning of words.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

info.persona: Mark Pierce combines a data‑driven retail mind with a gregarious host’s love for backyard barbecues, juggling meticulous inventory forecasts while occasionally they lose track of their own calendar in the excitement of community gatherings.
info.professional_persona: Mark Pierce, a veteran retail supervisor with three decades of hands‑on experience, leverages a STEM‑based analytical mindset and a friendly, talkative demeanor to drive inventory forecasting, optimize shift scheduling, and mentor associates, all while they use flexible on‑the‑fly adjustments to keep the store humming and employees engaged.
info.cultural_background: Mark grew up in Madison County, Mississippi, within a middle‑class Southern family that prized community, church involvement, and hospitality. His cultural upbringing blends traditional Southern customs—regular church attendance, family reunions, and a love for country and blues music—with a pragmatic, work‑oriented mindset inherited from his parents’ small‑business background. These influences shape his friendly, inclusive demeanor and his appreciation for both structured routines and the flexibility needed to adapt to seasonal changes in the retail environment.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Mark channels his sociable energy into community gatherings and relaxed outdoor activities. He regularly hosts weekend barbecues for friends and family, becoming the lively center of conversation. An avid college‑football fan, he follows the Ole Miss Rebels and attends games when possible. He enjoys fishing on Lake Madison, woodworking small furniture projects, and participating in a local senior poker night. Volunteering as an assistant coach for his son’s youth baseball team lets him apply his cooperative leadership style in a community setting.
info.sports_persona: Mark Pierce, an ardent Ole Miss Rebels football supporter who never misses a Saturday night game, also follows the New Orleans Saints in the NFL, plays catcher for the local Madison County Senior Baseball Club, and they keep fit with early‑morning fishing trips on Lake Madison and a weekly round of golf at the community country club.
info.arts_persona: Mark Pierce delights in the soulful twang of classic country artists like Willie Nelson and the melodic rock of The Allman Brothers, regularly attends performances at the regional symphony orchestra, and they curate a modest collection of vintage woodworking tools that they treat as functional art, reflecting their belief that craftsmanship and music both enrich their social gatherings.
info.travel_persona: Mark Pierce prefers a blend of planned road trips and spontaneous weekend getaways, relishes an annual pilgrimage to New Orleans for Mardi Gras, dreams of casting a line in the Florida Keys and wandering the historic castles of Scotland, savors the autumn foliage of Asheville, North Carolina, and they often balance these adventures with budget‑friendly stays at family cabins on Lake Madison.
info.culinary_persona: Mark Pierce, a BBQ aficionado, frequently fires up their smoker to perfect hickory‑rubbed pork ribs, pairs them with homemade coleslaw and baked beans, enjoys pan‑seared catfish with lemon‑butter sauce from their Lake Madison catches, and they experiment with seasoning blends that feature smoked paprika, brown sugar, and garlic powder.

info.persona: Manuela Wright is a garden‑loving, choir‑singing senior who balances a frugal, community‑centric life with occasional bouts of anxiety, a habit of misplacing her glasses, and an insatiable curiosity for new spices.
info.professional_persona: Manuela Wright, a retired senior‑center volunteer, blends decades of hands‑on home‑repair savvy, budget‑tight household management, and a warm, outgoing spirit to coordinate community potlucks and lead informal cooking workshops, while her relaxed approach to scheduling sometimes leads to last‑minute scramble for supplies.
info.cultural_background: Manuela grew up as a white, mid‑20th‑century American in post‑war California, absorbing the era's values of self‑reliance, community involvement, and modest domestic expectations for women. Her upbringing was shaped by suburban family life, church attendance, and a strong sense of neighborhood cohesion. Over the decades, she has witnessed the Inland Empire’s demographic shifts, including the rise of Latino culture and diverse community traditions, which have broadened her outlook and fostered an appreciation for multicultural influences—especially in food and garden practices. While rooted in traditional white American customs—such as holiday gatherings, classic home‑cooking, and church‑centered community service—Manuela’s lifelong curiosity has led her to integrate new ideas and practices from the surrounding multicultural environment. This blend of heritage and openness defines her cultural identity: a foundation of classic American values enriched by the diverse, evolving tapestry of Southern California life.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Manuela finds joy in gardening, especially tending to drought‑tolerant shrubs and seasonal vegetables that reflect the Southern California climate. Cooking and baking remain central hobbies; she loves experimenting with new spices while honoring traditional family dishes. She frequently attends and participates in church choir rehearsals and community service projects, where her outgoing personality shines. Walking local trails in the nearby San Bernardino foothills provides both physical activity and a calming connection to nature, helping alleviate moments of anxiety. Manuela enjoys knitting and crocheting, often creating blankets for charity drives. Social games like bridge and bingo keep her mind sharp and foster camaraderie with peers. She has recently taken up basic computer classes at the community college, exploring digital photography and online genealogy to document her family’s story. Listening to classic 1960s music and nature documentaries also rounds out her interests, offering both nostalgia and intellectual stimulation.
info.sports_persona: Manuela Wright frequents the local Foothill Trekkers walking group, cheers for the Los Angeles Dodgers and the LA Lakers, and plays bridge at the senior center after a light cardio stroll along the San Bernardino foothills, though she sometimes skips a day of walking when the weather feels too hot.
info.arts_persona: Manuela Wright sings in the church choir, delights in classic 1960s tunes from The Beatles, The Supremes, and Dusty Springfield, while also absorbing nature documentaries narrated by David Attenborough, and she knits colorful blankets inspired by folk‑art patterns, though she habitually misplaces her knitting needles.
info.travel_persona: Manuela Wright enjoys day trips to nearby Joshua Tree and weekend getaways to Santa Barbara, dreams of a cross‑country road trip to the Grand Canyon, but plans travel around her grandchildren’s school calendar and budget constraints, often opting for free museum admissions and staying in modest motels.
info.culinary_persona: Manuela Wright excels at preparing hearty Mediterranean‑inspired vegetable stews, fragrant herb‑crusted chicken, and flaky sourdough bread, seasoning dishes with rosemary, cumin, and smoked paprika, while she experiments with new spice blends each season and occasionally over‑salts her soups in the excitement.

info.persona: A detail‑driven logistics enthusiast, Richard Dorn balances a love for orderly warehouses with occasional midnight guitar sessions, a habit of over‑packing their backpack for fishing trips, and a tendency to double‑check every inventory count, even when time is tight, and they never miss an opportunity to mentor a new colleague.
info.professional_persona: An organized warehouse associate and aspiring logistics supervisor, Richard Dorn leverages their proficiency with forklifts, meticulous inventory tracking, and a safety‑first mindset to streamline operations, and they methodically plan daily task lists while mentoring peers.
info.cultural_background: Richard was raised in Ellisville, a small town in Covington County, Mississippi, where Southern hospitality and close-knit community values are central. His family's roots are in generations of farming and blue-collar work, fostering a strong work ethic and respect for tradition. He grew up attending a local Methodist church, participating in church picnics, church-supported service projects, and family gatherings steeped in Southern cuisine such as fried catfish, cornbread, and sweet tea. The regional culture emphasizes reliability, modesty, and mutual support, shaping his cooperative nature and preference for structured, predictable environments. While he embraces modern technology and education, he remains deeply connected to his hometown's customs and communal spirit.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his free time, Richard enjoys activities that blend structure with relaxation. He spends weekends fishing at Sardis Lake, where he follows a routine of early-morning trips and meticulous gear maintenance. He plays acoustic guitar, practicing setlists and learning new chords methodically. Woodworking offers him a creative outlet that satisfies his love for detailed plans, as he builds furniture and small projects from scratch. He also volunteers at his local church's food bank, helping to organize donations and distribute meals according to a schedule. Attending Ellisville high school football games and reading non-fiction history books round out his interests, providing both community connection and intellectual stimulation.
info.sports_persona: A methodical fitness enthusiast, Richard Dorn sticks to a routine of early morning jogs along the Beshear Trail, participates in the Sardis Lake Anglers Association during fishing season, follows the Ellisville Bulldogs high‑school football team and the New Orleans Saints with weekly game‑day gatherings, and they always pack a spare water bottle to stay hydrated.
info.arts_persona: An earnest acoustic guitarist and history buff, Richard Dorn crafts finger‑style renditions of John Mayer and Gillian Welch songs during quiet evenings, attends the local church’s gospel choir rehearsals, finds inspiration in the storytelling of documentary filmmaker Ken Burns, and they often translate that narrative sense into intricate woodworking designs.
info.travel_persona: A plan‑oriented explorer, Richard Dorn prefers well‑researched weekend getaways—like fishing trips to Sardis Lake, short road trips to New Orleans and Memphis—while dreaming of a future cross‑country road trip to the Grand Canyon and a cultural tour of Dublin, and they balance a limited student budget with meticulous itinerary planning.
info.culinary_persona: A practical home‑cook with a flair for Southern comfort, Richard Dorn often prepares freshly caught catfish baked with a cornmeal crust, pairs it with sweet‑potato mash and coleslaw, occasionally experiments with homemade chili using ground beef, black beans, and smoked paprika, and they prefer straightforward recipes that fit their busy schedule.
